limitations: Scaffold predicates are independently transcribed from primary chemistry figures, not fitted to the observed corpus reconstruction rate.
Identical acyl arms and fixed scaffold positions implement the delivered v8 family invariant. This does not prove experimental source-bank membership of a designed variant.
Jiang's head/site variants and Xue's designed tail variants retain computed-only evidence. Source route closure for their precursor syntheses is not admitted.

Xue Supplementary Fig. 12 draws a dihydroxy aldehyde input while showing triacylated products; Methods names the trihydroxy precursor but calls the acid heptanoic in an example named 2-methylhexanoate. Preserve this source conflict; no exact precursor-route execution is admitted.
These are complete net L1 transformations with source-reported condensation/reduction ordering. Transient protonation and reducing-agent speciation are not identified or claimed.
Jiang SI mislabels 6-oxohexyl oleate as 11 in the aldol procedure and calls palmitate octadecanoic acid elsewhere. Neither conflicting label enters the two oleate/linoleate final-assembly controls.
Designed v8 products are computed graph programs; experimental source-bank membership and exact precursor synthesis routes are not established.
Scaffold restrictions can exclude a corpus row but never authorize pruning an alternative forward product from a retained precursor tuple.
